projects.title: Autonomous CI/CD — AI-Driven Vulnerability Remediation Platform
projects.status: Prototype — functional pipeline, not yet running against live production repositories at scale
projects.description: An end-to-end platform that detects code vulnerabilities, generates patches with an LLM, validates them in isolated environments, and ships fixes through a human-in-the-loop approval gate — with full pipeline observability.
features: 10-node LangGraph state machine handling analysis, confidence grading, patch generation, parallel patch application, and memory updates — with crash-safe checkpointing at every stage.

Confidence grading engine that scores each fix on issue complexity, language-specific historical success rate, and pattern similarity before deciding whether to auto-generate a patch or escalate to a human.
Parallel patch application via LangGraph's Send API, splitting multi-file diffs into concurrent per-file workers instead of applying them serially.
Redis-backed webhook deduplication (1-hour TTL per commit SHA) to discard duplicate GitHub webhook retries before they trigger redundant pipeline runs.
Prompt-injection screening on vulnerability context before it reaches the LLM, plus HMAC-verified webhooks and JWT-scoped API endpoints.
Auto-provisioned Prometheus/Grafana stack tracking run duration percentiles, confidence scores, and patch failure rates per language out of the box.

codeSnippets.label: Pipeline graph definition (graph.py) — conditional routing between analysis, prediction, human approval, and parallel patch application
codeSnippets.code:
def route_after_prediction(state: PipelineState):
    """Routes based on prediction result."""
    if state.get("pipeline_status") == "ESCALATED":
        return "human_gate"
    return "fix_generator"

def build_pipeline_graph():
    workflow = StateGraph(PipelineState)
    workflow.add_node("analyzer", analyzer)
    workflow.add_node("prediction_engine", prediction_engine)
    workflow.add_node("fix_generator", fix_generator)
    workflow.add_node("human_approval_gate", human_approval_gate)
    workflow.add_node("patch_applier", patch_applier)
    workflow.add_node("file_worker", file_worker)
    workflow.add_node("patch_join", patch_join)
    workflow.add_node("evaluator", evaluator)
    workflow.add_node("memory_updater", memory_updater)
    workflow.add_node("human_gate", human_gate)

    workflow.add_edge(START, "analyzer")
    workflow.add_conditional_edges("analyzer", route_after_analyzer,
        {"fix_generator": "prediction_engine", "__end__": END})
    workflow.add_conditional_edges("prediction_engine", route_after_prediction,
        {"fix_generator": "fix_generator", "human_gate": "human_gate"})
    workflow.add_conditional_edges("patch_applier", patch_dispatcher,
        ["file_worker", "evaluator"])

    memory = MemorySaver()
    return workflow.compile(checkpointer=memory)

projects.title: Guardian AI — DDoS Detection & Mitigation System
projects.status: Prototype — full detect-and-mitigate loop runs end-to-end against simulated traffic; not deployed in front of live production infrastructure
projects.description: A real-time DDoS detection and mitigation system combining a feedforward classifier for attack fingerprinting with an LSTM for short-horizon risk prediction, wired directly into HAProxy for live rate-limit enforcement — plus a multi-vector attack simulator for validating detection accuracy.
features: Dual-model detection: a 4-layer feedforward network classifies traffic into 5 attack types (DNS amplification, HTTP flood, SYN flood, UDP flood, benign) with softmax confidence, while a 2-layer LSTM predicts near-term attack risk from time-series traffic features.
Live mitigation loop: a `/mitigation/toggle` endpoint calls into a custom HAProxyController to push real rate-limit rules onto the proxy, not just log a detection.
Model loading auto-detects input/output dimensions from saved weight shapes, falling back to freshly initialized weights with a logged warning if no trained model is found.

Built-in multi-vector attack simulator (HTTP flood, Slowloris, SYN flood, UDP flood, DNS amplification, and randomized mixed attacks) with a 10-worker thread pool, used to generate the traffic the detection models are validated against.
Prometheus metrics (total detections, recent attack count, last-attack confidence) exposed on a dedicated metrics port, separate from the Flask API port.

projects.title: Healthcare Multi-Portal SaaS — Cloud Architecture & Platform Skeleton
projects.status: Designed + Prototype — full K8s manifests and a working auth service exist; most services are scaffolded, auth uses a mock user store, and Postgres storage is non-persistent
projects.description: A full Kubernetes-native architecture and platform skeleton for a public healthcare coordination system — connecting citizens, clinics, and government health authorities through three role-separated portals on one backend.
features: 8 independently deployable, stateless microservices (auth, user/role, facility, request, government-ops, routing, metrics, audit) each with its own Kubernetes Deployment and ClusterIP Service.
Path-based Ingress routing all eight services through a single public endpoint while preserving service-level isolation.
Multi-cloud design split by responsibility: AWS for core compute/data, Azure for identity and governance, GCP for maps and analytics.
Region-scoped RBAC across five roles (citizen, clinic, government employee, government admin, platform admin), each with explicitly scoped permissions.
Request lifecycle management with 14-day auto-expiry, demand clustering, and route planning for government field visits.
Immutable audit logging and a 'no medical records stored' design constraint — built for visibility and coordination, not clinical data.
projects.note: Architecture and platform skeleton stage. Real Kubernetes Deployment/Service manifests and a working FastAPI auth service exist, but the auth service currently runs against a hardcoded mock user store (not a database), and Postgres storage is non-persistent (emptyDir) — both explicitly prototype-stage, not production.

codeSnippets.label: auth-deployment.yaml — real K8s Deployment + Service with readiness probe and ConfigMap/Secret injection
codeSnippets.code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: auth-deployment
  namespace: backend
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: auth-service
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: auth-service
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: auth-service
          image: auth-service:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8000
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: app-config
            - secretRef:
                name: app-secrets
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8000
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: auth-svc
  namespace: backend
spec:
  selector:
    app: auth-service
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 8000
  type: ClusterIP

projects.title: Dazai — Voice-Activated Workflow Launcher
projects.status: Production — runs daily as a personal dev-workflow tool
projects.description: A voice, clap, and hotkey-activated automation tool that sets up a full dev environment on command — launching Spotify, VS Code, and a dual-pane terminal pre-loaded with a local Ollama model and Claude Code.
features: Multi-trigger activation: wake-phrase detection, clap detection, and a global Ctrl+Shift+M hotkey.
One command boots the workspace: focus playlist on Spotify, VS Code, and a Windows Terminal split between an Ollama model and Claude Code.
Text-to-speech feedback via pyttsx3 with configurable voice, rate, and volume.
"Deafen/undeafen" mode to suspend voice-command listening during normal conversation without closing the app.
Runs persistently via Windows Startup integration with batch-script controls for start, stop, and restart.

codeSnippets.label: Workspace launcher (Dazai.py) — voice feedback, cascading fallbacks for launching VS Code, and a split-pane terminal with a local model + Claude Code
codeSnippets.code:
def start_dazai(skip_vscode=False):
    speak("Dazai online. A new day, another series of mundane tasks, no?")

    if not skip_vscode:
        speak("Launching VS Code")
        vscode_path = get_vscode_path()
        try:
            subprocess.Popen([vscode_path], shell=False,
                              creationflags=subprocess.CREATE_NO_WINDOW)
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Failed to launch VS Code with path '{vscode_path}': {e}")
            os.system("start code")

    speak("Loading your focus playlist on Spotify")
    open_spotify_and_play()

    speak("Initializing terminal with your AI companions.")
    terminal_cmd = [
        'wt',
        'new-tab', '-p', 'Command Prompt', 'cmd', '/k',
        'echo Starting Ollama... && ollama run qwen2.5:3b',
        ';',
        'new-tab', '-p', 'Command Prompt', 'cmd', '/k',
        'echo Starting Claude Code... && timeout /t 3 && claude'
    ]
    subprocess.Popen(terminal_cmd, shell=False,
                      creationflags=subprocess.CREATE_NO_WINDOW)

    speak("All systems are ready. Let's get to work.")
